newsitem.title: USA: EU okay of gene corn positive -- USDA's Glickman.
newsitem.headline: EU okay of gene corn positive -- USDA's Glickman.

text.p: The European Union took "a very positive step" by approving the sale of genetically altered corn, U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Wednesday.
"It's a very positive step. We're very happy about it," said Glickman, who was accompanied by a handful of Agriculture Department officials who were involved in the issue.

Undersecretary Gene Moos said the EU decision was welcome but USDA wanted to review the details, particularly on labeling. Trade adviser Paul Drazek said it appeared only seed corn would need a label identifying it as a biotech product.

Moos said USDA was "prepared and willing to work with the (European) Commission to take care of their concerns, as well as our concerns, to assure the smooth flow of corn exports to Europe." The EU is a sizable market for U.S. corn exports.

U.S. authorities approved use of the genetically altered corn months ago. It was grown on about 0.5 percent of U.S. corn acreage this year. Developed by Ciba-Geigy AG, the corn plant produces a biopesticide that repels the corn borer, a major pest.
Glickman, Moos and Drazek spoke during an impromptu interview with Reuters.

For the past several months, USDA officials, as well as grain merchandisers, have argued it would be cumbersome, expensive and impractical to require labeling of corn after harvest because it is transported in vast quantities and mingled with corn from many farms.

In an interview on Tuesday, Glickman and Drazek said they would examine any EU labeling requirement to see what impact it would have on trade. The labeling proposal that was to be presented to the European Commisson was "very complicated," Drazek said.
